A.explanation: A snapshot at one instant plots particle displacement parallel to travel against distance, which for a horizontal longitudinal wave is displacement to the right.

B.explanation: Particles in a longitudinal wave do not oscillate upwards, which is perpendicular to the horizontal direction of travel.

C.explanation: A time axis would show variation at one position over time, not a representation at one instant in time.

D.explanation: Time is wrong for a one-instant snapshot and upwards displacement is wrong for a horizontal longitudinal wave.

walkthrough: The stem states the wave is longitudinal and travels horizontally from left to right, and the graph is at one instant in time.
For a longitudinal wave, particle displacement is parallel to wave travel, so particles move horizontally to the left and right, not upwards.
At one instant in time the graph is a snapshot of many positions at the same time, so the $x$-axis must be distance along the wave, not time.
The $y$-axis must therefore show the horizontal particle displacement at each distance, with positive values meaning displaced to the right and negative values to the left.
This combination of distance and displacement of particles to the right matches row A. This is option A.
